content:
tomas_recruiter: FYI hiring manager wants to convert a contractor (6mo) to full-time w/ promotion to IC3. Director verbally approved title + comp target. What's the end-to-end for contractor -> FT + promo in one go? Any red flags?

chloe_manager: Congrats to the candidate! Key things: start date alignment, probation terms, and whether we treat prior contractor time as service for tenure/bonus. Also manager wants equity pro-rata from start date and a hiring bonus.

lina_hr: Good Q. Process: 1) Offer letter + comp approval (Recruit + Manager) 2) Submit Role Change packet after offer accepted (choose "new hire conversion/promote") 3) Comp will confirm banding and any panel needs 4) Payroll processes new hire onboarding and one-time payments.

­tomas_recruiter: We plan to have them start as FT on 2025-09-01. Contractor end date 2025-08-31. Manager wants backdated effective title to 2025-07-01 to account for work already done. Is that okay?

lina_hr: Backdating to while they were contractor is sensitive. We generally do NOT change base retroactively for contractor pay periods. We can make title effective 9/1 and offer a one-time conversion bonus to compensate prior work, or do a retroactive discretionary payment after they are on payroll but flagged as taxable. If you want effective comp earlier, it needs Legal review and hiring/contract documentation.

ammar_comp: From comp side: If you want IC3 banding, submit manager rationale + deliverables + market comps. Equity pro-rata: yes we can grant a prorated equity tranche with start date = FT start. If manager insists on vesting from contractor start, that's an exception and needs Comp + Legal signoff.

chloe_manager: Manager prefers pro-rata from 9/1. Okay with that. How to structure hiring bonus vs conversion payment so payroll handles taxes correctly?

michael_payroll: Best practice: 1) Put permanent base in offer (effective 9/1). 2) If you want to reward prior work, submit a one-time "Conversion Payment" via Compensation Adjustment referencing contractor ID and reason. In payroll, that will be taxed as supplemental income. For the hiring bonus, include pay period preference (e.g., first FT payroll).

lina_hr: Also note benefits eligibility: benefits and pension eligibility start date is FT start (9/1). If manager wants prior service counted for PTO accrual, include a request in packet and attach contractor payment records; People Ops will review but approval varies by jurisdiction.

ammar_comp: Checklist for comp submission: manager rationale (3 bullets), deliverables during contract, market comps, proposed base, bonus amount, equity grant details (amount, vesting start = 9/1), and note if any exceptions requested. If salary proposal exceeds band cap, Comp panel needed.

chloe_manager: Is there a faster path if candidate has competing offer and we need to expedite?

lina_hr: For expedite: label "expedite" in the Role Change packet, attach director + recruiter negotiation notes, and email comp@redwood with subject: "Expedite: Conversion + Promo | [Name] | Eff 2025-09-01". We can triage within 48 hours but approvals still required.

michael_payroll: Payroll cutoffs: to have pay + bonus in first FT pay period (starting 2025-09-01), we need finalized packet + payroll notice by 2025-08-20 EOD. One-time payments can be processed later but will tax in the period paid.

chloe_manager: About vacation and tenure: will they accrue vacation retroactively? Manager would like to credit prior contractor months for vacation accrual.

lina_hr: We can consider service credit for PTO on a case-by-case basis. Include contractor agreement + proof of hours in the packet. For US employees it's typically allowed; other countries may restrict. People Ops will confirm and document in offer letter if approved.

ammar_comp: Also check comp philosophy: external hires converted from contractor usually don't get salary retroactive increases; compensation is effective at FT start. Use one-time conversion payment to recognize prior contributions if needed.

chloe_manager: Good. Final Q: equity cliff or full pro-rata? Manager prefers a small "conversion grant" vesting over 4 years with 1-year cliff starting 9/1. Is that standard?

ammar_comp: Standard: new FT grants follow normal vesting (4y/1y cliff) starting at FT date. For converted contractors, we typically pro-rate the grant to reflect start (so vesting start = 9/1). If you want to waive cliff or alter schedule that's special exception. Document request in Equity Recommendation form.

people-ops-bot: Reminder checklist: Required Role Change/new-hire conversion fields: employee name, employee ID (if known), current contractor role, proposed FT title, proposed base, effective FT date, manager rationale, director approval, budget code, equity instruction (pro-rate yes/no), hiring/one-time payment amount and pay period. Links: Offer templates https://recruiting.redwood.internal/offer-templates, Role Change portal https://hr.redwood.internal/role-change, Equity request https://comp.redwood.internal/equity-request, Payroll deadlines https://payroll.redwood.internal/deadlines

chloe_manager: Thanks all, we'll proceed with offer + mark Role Change as conversion. I'll attach contractor docs and request pro-rata equity. Will ping when offer signed. :+1:
